clue.text: Music comes from this plumbing behind the basin

indicators.note: behind puts the plumbing word after the basin word in the answer

parts.note: a pan is a shallow basin or dish
pipes are what plumbing is made of

explanation.surface: A remark that a tune is coming out of the pipes under the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' sets the plumbing word after the basin word. The definition is a descriptive phrase for an instrument, not a single synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument is a row of reed pipes blown across to produce a tune.

clue.text: Estrange with a fib neat construction

parts.note: a fib is a small lie

indicators.note: construction means the letters of neat are built into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone drives people apart by building a tidy little untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' looks like a noun about building something; it is the anagram signal on 'neat' only, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to turn them away from one another, making them hostile or distant.

clue.text: Married couple worked hand-in-glove to amuse the kids

definitions.text: Married couple worked hand-in-glove to amuse the kids

parts.words: Married couple worked hand-in-glove to amuse the kids
parts.note: the husband-and-wife pair of a seaside show are glove puppets, literally worked by a hand inside them, for children's entertainment

explanation.surface: A husband and wife collaborate closely to entertain children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand-in-glove' usually means in close partnership; here it is literal, as these are glove puppets from a traditional British seaside puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional puppet show stars a quarrelsome husband and wife, operated as glove puppets for children.

clue.text: Dialect peculiar to Pisa

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of to Pisa are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A remark that some local speech is found only in Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar to' reads as 'unique to', but 'peculiar' is the anagram signal working on TO PISA.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional, non-standard form of speech.

clue.text: Announces 22 on board

indicators.note: on, with board, means sitting inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is aboard
the answer to 22 down means 'ever', which is AY in old poetic usage

explanation.surface: Someone declares the answer to clue 22 while aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: An archaic word for 'ever' matches 22-down's answer; 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to state it out loud, to declare it.

clue.text: Classic age, I not so great

parts.note: an age is a period of time
something not so great is less

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that a person and their era are past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic work never dates, staying admired across generations.

clue.text: Some home tuition for housewife

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A homemaker receives a bit of private teaching at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for housewife' as the definition, but 'for' is a link word: 'housewife' alone is the old name for a small sewing kit, which is the needle case meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewife (pronounced 'hussif') is a small sewing case, and this is a small ornamental case for needles.

clue.text: It's not fair describing her colouring

definitions.text: It's not fair describing her colouring

parts.words: It's not fair describing her colouring
parts.note: fair here means light-haired, so the woman's hair colour is the opposite of fair

explanation.surface: A complaint that a description of a woman's complexion is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' sounds like a protest at injustice; it means not blonde, i.e. dark-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair is not fair-haired.

clue.text: No government supporter makes such stirring speeches

definitions.text: No government supporter makes such stirring speeches

parts.words: No government supporter makes such stirring speeches
parts.note: a rabble-rouser opposed to those in power gives rousing talks that stir up trouble

explanation.surface: An opponent of the government delivers rousing orations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like praise for fine oratory; it means stirring up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser stirs up public feeling against the authorities.

clue.text: Family saving money for oven

indicators.note: saving means keeping hold of, so the money sits inside the family word

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
L is the abbreviation for pound, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Relatives put money aside to buy a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means holding: KIN keeps L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a furnace for firing pottery or drying materials.

clue.text: Fair sample of angry group

parts.note: cross means angry
a section is a group or division

explanation.surface: A representative selection taken from a furious crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a representative slice of a population.

clue.text: A call for judgment, with this winning card to play?

explanation.surface: Someone holding the deciding card waits for a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the trumpet blast heralding the biblical Day of Judgment; the other is the final trump card in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet sounding on Judgment Day calls the dead to be judged, and a final high card in a hand can take the trick.

clue.text: Goaded donkey raced around

indicators.note: around means the racing word goes round the animal

parts.note: hared means ran fast
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey was provoked into running in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goaded donkey' reads as one phrase, but 'Goaded' alone is the definition and 'around' wraps the racing word round the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goaded and harassed both mean pestered or tormented repeatedly.

clue.text: Teacher or patron

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A choice between a teacher and a sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or support, as a patron does.

clue.text: Cast off

parts.note: the actors leave the stage, read as a stage direction

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin stage direction means 'they go out', marking the actors' departure.

clue.text: Provide strong con-elusion

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Something gives a powerful finish.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for forte, the musical marking for 'loud'. To fend for someone is to provide for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fend, as in fend for oneself, is to look after or supply.

clue.text: For me, sea when rough is terrifying

indicators.note: rough means turbulent, so the letters of for me sea are churned up

explanation.surface: Someone finds the ocean frightening in stormy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means frightening, causing dread.

clue.text: Note return of sun: sign to take something off

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: return of means the word sun is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A memo about the sun coming back, with a sign to remove something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written memo; it is a sol-fa note. 'return of' turns the word sun backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction symbol tells you to deduct one amount from another.

clue.text: Am over to stay, but pretend to be ill

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word Am is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to linger is to stay on

explanation.surface: A visitor stays on but fakes sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AM into MA.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign sickness to avoid work.

clue.text: Partially-collapsed area of church

indicators.note: partially means only part of the next word is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Part of a church has fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partially-collapsed' reads as one adjective, but 'Partially' says take part of 'collapsed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Authorise penalty

explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve officially; a sanction is also a punishment imposed for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Flower book for Christmas, perhaps

explanation.surface: A garden plant and a seasonal gift volume.
explanation.walkthrough: An ANNUAL is a plant living one year, and a yearly hardback for children often given at Christmas in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant completing its life cycle in one year, and a book published yearly, often a Christmas present.

clue.text: Suffering after-effects of poor catering?

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters of catering are mangled

explanation.surface: Feeling ill after bad food at a function.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting badly means showing symptoms in response to something taken in.

clue.text: Invariably, this Irish county's short of a leader

indicators.note: short of a leader means the first letter is dropped from the county word

parts.note: Galway is a county in the west of Ireland, with possessive S

explanation.surface: A claim that an Irish county is always missing its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: GALWAY'S loses its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariably means every time, without exception.

clue.text: Determination of the protected tenant?

parts.note: a renter with legal protection has the right to remain in the home, and endurance is the other sense

explanation.surface: Asking about the resolve of a tenant with security of tenure.
explanation.walkthrough: A protected tenant in Britain has a legal right to stay in their rented home, so has the power of staying.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or stamina is the ability to keep going.

clue.text: Colleague means every thing to you at first

parts.note: all means every thing

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Telling someone their workmate is everything to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate on your side.

clue.text: See me work up an ode, say

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the words me and work are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Asking someone to watch as I compose an ode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the run ME + OP to give PO + EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is one example of a piece of verse.

clue.text: Team of one?

parts.note: a team is a group, and a group consisting of just one thing is single in number

explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a group acting together, and also the number one.

clue.text: Italian motorway and country roads heading east

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
lanes are narrow country roads
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Driving through Italy from the motorway onto rural roads heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is a British motorway; the figure 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Milan is Milanese, so Italian.

clue.text: Girl locked up, having been extravagant

parts.note: a miss is a girl
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: A young woman was confined after overspending.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that has been squandered or wasted was spent wrongly, as by an extravagant person.
